title: Francesca Albanese: Driven by a strong sense of justice
text:
Photo: Supplied: Hardie Grant Publishing

Italian human rights lawyer Francesca Albanese is the United Nations special rapporteur on Palestinian territories - a role that has seen her sanctioned by the United States and both revered and criticized internationally.

Her 2024 report Anatomy of a Genocide accused world leaders of a lack of empathy for Palestinians and claimed the threshold for the crime of genocide had been met in Gaza.

She was critical not only of Israel, but of other nations failure to impose sanctions on Israel. 

Israel was quick to dismiss her findings and its ally, the United States, named Ms Albanese a 'specially designated national' - placing her among the likes of Vladimir Putin.

Her US assets were frozen and US nationals were banned from doing business with her.

She has been called antisemitic and was also threatened with arrest in Germany for using a controversial slogan that some believe has a genocidal intent to eliminate the Israeli state.

Ms Albanese talks about all of this in her new book, When the World Sleeps.

A US federal judge recently temporarily blocked US sanctions against her, finding that the Trump administration likely violated her free speech rights by imposing the measures.

The US government has appealed the ruling.
